what:
## fastcompile-macros 7: cargo: a proc-macro unit builds no native code (every proc-macro build fails today)

Where: `crates/blaze-cargo/src/serve/unit/compile.rs` `fn names` (`builds_code`, line ~471), which `fn generate` and `fn assemble` read.

What is wrong: a proc-macro unit has `builds_code: true`, so `codegen::generate` runs it with `RootKind::ProcMacro`. `HirFrontend::roots` then calls `roots::proc_macros::roots`, which refuses any crate whose root file has no `__blaze_proc_macros` module ("its root file has no list of its proc macros"), and nothing in the v2 daemon appends that module (`proc_macro_list` has no caller; only test harnesses are appended, `unit/harness.rs`). So `generated` is `Err`, `assemble` returns `ok: false`, and `fn macros` (compile.rs:663) loads no expanders: every crate that uses a proc macro fails, though `blaze_macro_eval::load` is wired and ready.

What: `builds_code` false for a proc-macro unit (`u.target.is_proc_macro()`), as for an inert build script. Under change 20 (docs/v2/plan/design/compile-time.md) nothing loads a proc macro's native image: `blaze_macro_eval::load` runs the macro's MIR from the front end, and its compiled tier compiles from MIR itself. Building the image is wasted work and, today, the failure above. `ok` then comes from the unit's check alone, which is what `fn macros` should be given. Its outputs are `artifact::made(plan)` (the `None` arm of `assemble`), as for any unit that compiles no code.

Not instead appending the list module: that keeps a native build nothing loads.

history.note: serve/unit/compile.rs names(): builds_code is false for a proc-macro lib (codegen::makes == Shared { proc_macro: true }); its lib test (Mode::Test, Makes::Executable) still builds. ok comes from its check, outputs are artifact::made(plan), and macros() loads its expanders through blaze_macro_eval::load. The list module is no longer appended: serve/unit/harness.rs writes only test harnesses (proc_macro_root deleted), and blaze-lower lib.rs gives only a harnessed test an alias root, so a proc macro root is its file on disk. Tests: serve::unit::tests::a_proc_macros_root_is_its_file_on_disk_and_its_def_map_has_its_macros, blaze_lower tests the_lib_of_a_proc_macro_is_one_unit_under_build_and_test and an_edit_of_a_root_file_reaches_every_root_of_it rewritten. RootKind::ProcMacro and HirFrontend::proc_macro_list now have no caller in the daemon (queued to codegen).
